author_prompt:
Author 8 DIFFERENT natural ecommerce customer-service dialogue families in en.
Batch 0; ensure at least four current turns classified as general across this batch.
Each family has its OWN coherent history of 2, 4 or 6 short alternating user/assistant
messages, followed by 3 ALTERNATIVE current user turns, not three sequential turns.
Those alternatives differ in effective intent: retain vs replace, withdraw vs
continue, single goal vs concurrent goal, or resolved vs unresolved reference.
Include natural short answers where history matters. Vary old completed tasks,
hesitation, self-correction, indirect wording, topics and dialogue acts. General
and human-service requests must also occur as NEW goals, not only stale history.
Do not follow a repeated sentence template or substitute product nouns to create
new families. Avoid stereotyped 'information only, do not submit' repetition.
Invent broad everyday ecommerce situations; no copied benchmark or private data.
History plus current turn should fit 150 English words or 180 Chinese characters;
keep it compact but meaningful. No future replies or final conversation summaries.
Supply the correct label for each alternative according to the rubric.

families.scenario: Customer asks about a smartwatch they bought and then shifts to a general question.

messages.content: Hi, I got the FitPulse S2 watch yesterday. The heart-rate monitor seems off.
Sorry to hear that. Have you tried wearing it snugly above the wrist bone?
Yes, I did that. It still reads about 20 bpm lower than my chest strap.
That's a known calibration quirk. Let me check if a firmware update is available for your unit.

variants.text: Actually, forget the watch issue. Do you folks have a physical store in Chicago?
variants.label: general

variants.text: Okay, please go ahead and push the firmware update to my device.
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Wait, actually I'd rather return it. Can you start a return for me?
variants.label: billing_refund

families.scenario: Customer asks about delivery of a desk lamp and then makes a small-talk remark.

messages.content: I ordered the LumaGlow desk lamp on Monday. Order #88412.
Thanks! That order is scheduled to arrive this Friday by 8 PM.
Great. Can you also tell me if the lamp comes with a UK plug adapter?
It ships with a universal adapter, so yes, UK plugs are covered.

variants.text: Perfect, thanks for the quick help. Have a nice day!
variants.label: general

variants.text: Hmm, but I'm moving next week. Can I change the delivery address to my new place?
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Actually, I realize I need two lamps, not one. Can I add another to this order?
variants.label: order_logistics

families.scenario: Customer asks about a refund for a returned jacket, then asks about store hours.

messages.content: I returned the waterproof jacket two weeks ago. Tracking says it was delivered to your warehouse.
Let me look that up. I see the return was received on the 3rd.
Okay, so when will the money hit my card? It's been a while.
Refunds typically process within 5-7 business days after receipt. Yours should post by the 12th.

variants.text: Got it, I'll keep an eye out. By the way, are you open on Sundays?
variants.label: general

variants.text: It's the 14th now and I still don't see it. Can you escalate this?
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Actually, I changed my mind — I want the jacket back instead of the refund. Can you reverse it?
variants.label: billing_refund

families.scenario: Customer asks about account login trouble, then asks a product question.

messages.content: I can't log into my account. It says my password is wrong.
Let's reset it. I've sent a reset link to your email on file.
I clicked it and set a new password, but now it says my account is locked.
That happens after too many failed attempts. I've unlocked it now — try again in a minute.

variants.text: Thanks, that worked. While I'm here, do you sell replacement bands for the FitPulse S1?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Thanks, that worked. I appreciate your patience with all this.
variants.label: general

variants.text: Actually, I think someone else might be using my account. Can you check recent logins?
variants.label: account_security

families.scenario: Customer asks about a coffee grinder order and then asks for a human agent.

messages.content: My order #5521 for the BurrMaster grinder shows delivered, but I never got it.
I'm sorry about that. The carrier marked it as left at the front door on Tuesday.
I checked with my neighbors and the leasing office. Nobody has it.
I can file a claim with the carrier. Would you like me to start that process?

variants.text: Yes, please start the claim. Also, can you tell me if the grinder has a ceramic burr?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: No, I've had enough of this. Put me through to a real person right now.
variants.label: human_service

variants.text: Actually, never mind — it just showed up. My neighbor had it all along. Thanks anyway!
variants.label: general

families.scenario: Customer asks about a subscription renewal charge they don't recognize.

messages.content: I was charged $39 for something called 'Nimbus Plus' but I never signed up for that.
Let me check. I see a Nimbus Plus subscription was activated on your account last month.
That's strange. I only bought a one-time cloud storage pack from you.
It looks like the one-time pack auto-renewed into a monthly plan. I can cancel and refund it.

variants.text: Please cancel it and refund the charge. I don't want any subscription.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Hold on — if I keep it, does the $39 include the 2TB tier or just 1TB?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Actually, my wife might have signed up from her phone. Let me check with her first.
variants.label: __DEFER__

families.scenario: Customer asks about a damaged speaker and then asks about warranty coverage.

messages.content: My BoomPod Mini arrived with a cracked casing. I just unboxed it today.
Oh no. Since it arrived damaged, we can send a replacement at no cost.
Good. But I'm traveling next week — can you hold the replacement until I'm back?
Sure, I can schedule the shipment for after your return date. Just confirm the date.

variants.text: Let's do it — ship it on the 20th. And does the replacement come with a fresh warranty?
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Actually, you know what, I'd rather just get my money back instead of a replacement.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Hmm, actually I'm not sure I want to keep it at all. Can I think about it and get back to you?
variants.label: __DEFER__

families.scenario: Customer asks about a pet feeder order and then asks about a different product.

messages.content: I ordered the AutoMunch pet feeder, order #9033. It's been 10 days and no shipping update.
I see it's still at the warehouse — there was a stock delay on the 3L version.
Ugh, I needed it before my trip. Is there any way to speed this up?
I can upgrade you to express shipping once it's ready, at no extra cost.

variants.text: Fine, but I'm leaving Friday. If it can't arrive by then, just cancel the order.
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Thanks for offering. Honestly, I'm just stressed about my trip — is it usually this busy for you guys?
